bug_semantics: An authenticated caller can choose another tenant's supplier ID in PUT /api/supplier/{id}. SupplierUpdateController resolves it globally with Supplier::find($id), SupplierRequest authorizes only Auth::check(), and update($request->all()) mass-assigns arbitrary body keys against Supplier::$fillable, which includes company_id. The caller can therefore read the returned foreign supplier, modify it, and reassign it to the caller's company.
flaw_origin: The PR member commit 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee changed the previously empty update method into the flawed unscoped lookup plus whole-body mass assignment and created the authentication-only SupplierRequest. Its controller blob was carried byte-for-byte into squash merge b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369, which set APP_VERSION to 4.0.0. The PUT route was not present in that squash's routes/api.php; b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403 later published the already-flawed method at version 4.15.0. Thus 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee is the smallest code-writing BIC, while route activation is a later lifecycle event.
ai_marker: absent — the raw 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee commit object names Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com> as both author and committer and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer
evidence: The first-party CNA page https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-78365-idor-supplier-api-cross-tenant-update identifies SupplierUpdateController::update(), Supplier::find($id), update($request->all()), fillable company_id, Auth::check(), PUT /api/supplier/{id}, affected versions through 5.3.1, and patch 4a52477e6ed66afa436814c80e7bcd68670dd596.

refs/pull/227/head resolves to 63c504abd35cc721e7cf94ed47b7426b1f938485. git log --reverse over the reconstructed PR series identifies member 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee ('refactor(api): Refactor Supplier endpoint') as the commit that implemented the update method; git show of that member adds Supplier::find($id), update($request->all()), the JSON response, and SupplierRequest::authorize() returning Auth::check().

git rev-parse 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee:app/Http/Controllers/Api/Supplier/SupplierUpdateController.php b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369:app/Http/Controllers/Api/Supplier/SupplierUpdateController.php returns the same blob f4829388d8ba029bc1356d915c061866656265cc for both, proving the decomposed member's flawed controller landed unchanged in the squash.

Lifecycle/version cross-check: b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369:version.php is 4.0.0 and v2.0.1:version.php is also 4.0.0, so the flawed code precedes the advisory's lower bound. However, the complete b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369 routes/api.php has no supplier PUT route. git show b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403 -- routes/api.php proves that commit first adds Route::put('/supplier/{id}', ...) over parent 7f05ac6d115c09dc570e002b28e126871057333e, and b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403:version.php is 4.15.0. The advisory's 4.0.0 lower bound therefore describes dormant vulnerable code; the stated HTTP attack path becomes reachable at 4.15.0.

git show 4a52477e6ed66afa436814c80e7bcd68670dd596 changes version.php from 5.3.1 to 5.3.2, scopes lookup to Supplier::where('company_id', Auth::user()->company_id)->find($id), replaces request->all() with request->validated(), and requires create/update supplier permission. git merge-base of b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369 and the fix is b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369. git tag --contains the fix returns v5.5.3 and v5.14.0, agreeing that 5.3.2 is untagged and v5.5.3 is the first tagged fixed release.

git cat-file commit 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee gives parent 37af4daadbfec766fc691555a1f124b376bd33ae, human author/committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, and a message with no trailers. This is the only commit object used for the AI judgment.
reasoning: The security defect is the combination written in 3cef95157121a1bb5de24253d23130c7d0a38bee: authentication without tenant/permission authorization, an attacker-controlled global primary-key lookup, and whole-body mass assignment to a model where company_id is fillable. The immediate parent contains an empty method, so direct parent-tree inspection proves absence. PR #227 was squash-merged, but its preserved head reconstructs the smaller member commit, and identical controller blob IDs prove that member's vulnerable body is exactly what landed in b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369; the squash aggregate is therefore not the BIC. The body existed from the 4.0.0 squash, although historical routes show the described HTTP endpoint was dormant until the supplier PUT route was added at version 4.15.0. It remained flawed through 5.3.1 and was directly fixed in 4a52477e6ed66afa436814c80e7bcd68670dd596 for 5.3.2; v5.5.3 is the first tag containing that fix. Finally, the BIC's raw commit object has a human author and committer and no AI marker. Under the required BIC-only attribution rule, later lifecycle commits cannot alter the result, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
